plan.title: Genotype x drug interaction DE + pathway enrichment (heart)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq experiment (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 16 samples, 12000 genes, Salmon-derived raw counts) in heart tissue. The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is a genotype x treatment interaction question. We fit PyDESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment (Python-only, per user constraint), explicit reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle). To report the interaction and both simple effects as single, directly Wald-testable and apeglm-shrinkable model coefficients (avoiding a linear-combination contrast that PyDESeq2 does not natively support and that would otherwise require R's ashr), we fit the same formula twice: once with genotype releveled to WT (giving the WT simple drug effect and the interaction coefficient directly) and once with genotype releveled to KO (giving the KO simple drug effect directly, since the interaction coefficient is invariant to which genotype is the reference for its own significance test). QC precedes modeling to catch batch or outlier problems before any test runs. Low-count filtering is minimal (independent filtering does the rest). LFC shrinkage uses PyDESeq2's native apeglm-style single-coefficient shrinkage for all three reported quantities, since each is now a single model coefficient by construction. BH-adjusted results per contrast feed a preranked GSEA (gseapy) against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome (both HGNC-symbol GMTs matching the counts' gene-symbol identifiers, so no Entrez remapping is needed), ranked on the Wald statistic, run separately per contrast per rule against pooling contrasts. A synthesis report presents the three results side by side (WT simple effect, KO simple effect, interaction) with diagnostics, leading-edge genes, and the low-power caveat that n=4/cell interaction tests have low sensitivity.
